label: UniFi Dream Machine Pro
description: UniFi Dream Machine Pro (UDM-Pro) - 1U UniFi OS console: 1x 1G RJ45 WAN + 8x 1G RJ45 LAN (no PoE), and 2x 10G SFP+ cages, one wired as WAN and one as LAN. 3.5 Gbps IDS/IPS, 33 W max.
notes:
Census is the vendor datasheet's own interface rows, text layer read 2026-11-19: 'Networking interface (8) LAN: GbE RJ45 ports / (1) WAN: GbE RJ45 port' and 'SFP+ interface (1) LAN: 10G SFP+ / (1) WAN: 10G SFP+' - 9x 1G copper plus 2x 10G cages, and no PoE. https://dl.ui.com/ds/udm-pro.pdf (200, 353,553 B, application/pdf, 2 pp). The tech-spec page prints the same count as a table, '1 GbE RJ45 = 9 (1G/100M/10M)' and '10G SFP+ = 2 (10G/1G)', and its Datasheet button points at the same PDF: https://techspecs.ui.com/unifi/cloud-gateways/udm-pro (200, 676,527 B) - both read 2026-11-19. Note the URL naming trap this model exposes: dl.ui.com/ds/udm-pro.pdf is the datasheet, while dl.ui.com/ds/udm-pro_ds.pdf - the suffix many other Ubiquiti datasheets use - answers 302 to the techspecs front page.

Replaced two earlier entries that described this one box twice: devices/ubiquiti/UDM-Pro.json modelled the second 10G cage as a bare 'ethernet 10G' port with no connector, so the box had one cage and a 10G port nothing can seat in, and devices/ubiquiti/unifi-dream-machine-pro.json carried the right port count under model 'UniFi Dream Machine Pro' (a product name, not a model), category 'host' and the engine's 'host' capability - which means an end device that terminates packets (engine/device.js), not a console that hosts apps - on a gateway. One model, one file: the aliases keep both spellings searchable. Capability set follows the rest of the Dream Machine line (UDM-Pro-Max, UDM-SE): no 'host'.

PoE re-checked 2026-11-19: both vendor surfaces say this console does not accept PoE. https://techspecs.ui.com/unifi/cloud-gateways/udm-pro (HTTP 200, 676,527 B) prints Port Layout (9) 1 GbE & (2) 10G SFP+, Max. Power Consumption 33 W, Power Method '(1) Universal AC input, 100-240V AC, 50/60 Hz / (1) USP-RPS DC input', Power Supply 'AC/DC, internal, 50W', and no PoE row whatsoever (zero occurrences of 'PoE' or '802.3'). https://store.ui.com/us/en/products/udm-pro (HTTP 200, 600,589 B): PoE Support flag Empty, PoE Budget flag Empty, Max. PoE Wattage per Port by PSE Empty, Power Method as above. All nine copper ports now say poeIn: false - isPoePd() matches 'unifi' in the label, and without the explicit false each silent port drew 12.95 W 802.3af: 116.55 W of phantom load on a gateway with a 50 W internal AC/DC supply and no PSE. The two 10G cages are SFP+ and carry no PoE either way.

**LAN bank (layer 2), read 2026-11-21.** Both vendor surfaces print the same three rows: `MAC Address Table Size = 4,000`, `LACP Port Aggregation = True` with the note "GbE RJ45 ports 1-8", and `VLAN/Subnet-based Traffic Segmentation = True` - https://techspecs.ui.com/unifi/cloud-gateways/udm-pro (HTTP 200, 676,527 B), and the storefront's own payload repeats each row at https://store.ui.com/us/en/products/udm-pro (HTTP 200, 600,722 B). A 4,000-entry MAC table is a bridge forwarding database, and a LAG over the eight 1G sockets cannot be built from routed ports, so Port 1-Port 8 forward at layer 2 and the row declares `l2-forward` (MAC learning + flooding only; VLAN, LAG and STP ride on it). Measured on the pre-change spec: hosts on Port 1 and Port 2 in 192.168.1.0/24 could not resolve each other's ARP, and `switchport access vlan 10` answered "cannot switch frames: it has no l2-forward capability". `no switchport` still makes a LAN port routed; the WAN port keeps its address. This supersedes the 'no l2-forward' clause in the sentence above, which copied the Dream Machine line's capability set before the sibling UDM-Pro-Max was read; it publishes the same rows and was fixed in PR #2334.

WAN/LAN separation, read 2026-11-21. Ubiquiti's controller device database numbers the sockets and names the uplink: https://static.ui.com/fingerprint/ui/public.json (HTTP 200, 832,585 B, `devices` entry with `sku` = UDM-Pro) prints `ports` = {"eth0": "LAN", "eth1": "LAN", "eth2": "LAN", "eth3": "LAN", "eth4": "LAN", "eth5": "LAN", "eth6": "LAN", "eth7": "LAN", "eth8": "WAN", "eth9": "WAN2", "eth10": "LAN", "plus": [10, 11], "standard": 9} with `numberOfPorts` 11 - nine RJ45 sockets, the ninth the uplink, then the two 10G cages. The product page repeats the split in words: "Default WAN Ports (1) 10G SFP+ / (1) GbE RJ45", beside "1 GbE RJ45 = 9 (1G/100M/10M)", "10G SFP+ = 2 (10G/1G)" and "MAC Address Table Size = 4,000" at https://techspecs.ui.com/unifi/cloud-gateways/udm-pro (HTTP 200, 676,527 B, read 2026-11-21). `role` is the field `engine/device.js` `ownsIpOn` reads ("WAN and LAN are separate L3 surfaces ... role separation outranks the VLAN shortcut"), and it fires only when BOTH sides carry one, so a LAN bank with no role leaves the invariant this repo already asserts for the RT-AX89X (test/port-roles.test.js, "the WAN port does not answer the LAN address") silently false: with 192.168.1.1/24 on port1, `ownsIpOn(wan1, '192.168.1.1')` returned the LAN interface, i.e. a host cabled to wan1 inside that subnet was answered by the LAN gateway. wan1 now declares role "wan" and port1 through port8 "lan"; measured after the change, wan1 no longer owns the LAN address, port2 still reaches the address held on port1 (the bank still answers bank-wide), and wan1 still answers an address of its own. The two SFP+ cages keep their names and no `role`: the datasheet prints one LAN and one WAN cage without numbering them, so which of `sfp1`/`sfp2` is the WAN cage is not a wiring fact this catalogue can state - the same restraint `udw.json` records for its cages. Gate: test/ubiquiti-wan-lan-role-separation.test.js.
